subject: [PATCH 2/6] daxctl: online whole-device memory atomically when available

2026-10-16.patch_summary: This patch modifies the daxctl tool to online whole-device memory atomically when available, rather than onlining each block separately. This approach avoids racing issues with other agents that may be online blocks as they appear. The kernel's daxX.Y/state is used to determine if a device is offline and can be unplugged, allowing for atomic onlineing of the entire device. If another agent has already onlineed memory from the device, the patch will fall back to the per-block path. Additionally, the patch now fails when attempting to online a device with no memory blocks, rather than reporting zero sections already online.

reviews.author: Alison Schofield
reviews.summary:
Reviewer noted that using DAXCTL_KMEM_ONLINE in the atomic --no-movable path could place memory in ZONE_MOVABLE despite --no-movable, and suggested either changing it to DAXCTL_KMEM_ONLINE_KERNEL or adding a zone check

Reviewer noted that a reconfigure-device command may add memory twice, first offline at probe and then daxctl unplugs it and adds it back online, leaving the device unplugged if the re-add fails. Alison suggested transitioning directly from offline to an online state instead of falling back to per-block onlining.
reviews.raw_body:
Hi Greg, 

A couple of things here...

The atomic --no-movable path uses DAXCTL_KMEM_ONLINE, leaving zone selection
to the kernel. With memory_hotplug.online_policy=auto-movable, IIUC this could
place memory in ZONE_MOVABLE despite --no-movable.

The per-block path checks the resulting zone and fails if it isn't ZONE_NORMAL,
but the atomic path skips that check.

Should this use DAXCTL_KMEM_ONLINE_KERNEL instead, or retain DAXCTL_KMEM_ONLINE
and add the same zone check?

---

With this, a "reconfigure-device -m system-ram" may add the memory twice.
First kmem adds it offline at probe and then daxctl unplugs it and adds it
back online. If that re-add fails, the device is left unplugged rather than
offline.

I get that falling back to per-block onlining would reopen the race this
series is addressing. Could the kernel interface support transitioning
directly from offline to an online state instead? It seems that would avoid
both the extra hotplug work and the left-unplugged failure case.

-- Alison

2026-10-21.patch_summary: This patch modifies the daxctl device control tool to online whole-device memory atomically when available, rather than onlining each block individually. This approach avoids racing issues with other agents that may be online blocks as they appear. The kernel only onlines from an 'unplugged' state, and if this fails (e.g., due to lack of hotremove support), the device is left unchanged and onlined per-block. The patch also updates the per-block path to fail when a device has no memory blocks, rather than reporting zero sections already online.

reviews.author: Gregory (Meta) (author)
reviews.summary:
Author acknowledged that concurrent block/state changes could make blocks unrecoverable, confirming this was the intended behavior.

Author acknowledges a technical limitation in their patch due to backward compatibility concerns and expresses willingness to explore alternative solutions, but no clear resolution or fix is planned.
reviews.raw_body:
This was the intended behavior because otherwise a concurrent
block/state change would end up making the blocks unrecoverable.

---

This is an unfortunate wart for backward compatibility sake.  It would
have been preferable to create the dax device without auto-hotplugging
the kmem region (hotplug but offline), but that would break userspace.

I can take another look whether i can get offline->online to work
internally, but this may still require the hotplug work you're concerned
about.

-- 
~Gregory
